items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: The bandoleen was half violin and half banjo, made by Felon Harlen

ctx.x: Yes, yes. And, Bubber was the main stay. He created the style for that band, he and Charlie Ervis. While I'm on the subject of the origin of Duke's style, I would also like to mention the type of bands that were in New York in those days in the very early '20's, the dance halls -- you had bands of 30 and 40 and 50 pieces, and they were composed of banjos, bandeleens, violins, trumpets, trumbones, maybe one or two saxiphones. Saxophone hadn't been quite popular then. The bandoleen was half violin and half banjo,…
a head like a banjo, called a bandoleen.
